annotation_description: Sacrificed Lotus Petal to cast Ponder when Polluted Delta could have fetched an Island to provide the blue mana instead. Lotus Petal is a flexible, one-shot mana source that could have been preserved for future turns (e.g., enabling Dark Ritual + Cabal Ritual lines or providing off-color mana).

chosen_display: Polluted Delta — {T}, Pay 1 life, Sacrifice {this}: Search your li... [Activate]
annotation_description: Activated Polluted Delta while their own Ponder was on the stack. This shuffles the library before Ponder resolves, losing the ability to see the top 3 cards first and then decide whether to shuffle (via Ponder's own shuffle clause) or keep them arranged. The correct sequence is to let Ponder resolve, look at the top 3, and then use the fetch afterward if needed to shuffle away unwanted cards left on top.

Cast Dark Ritual with Ponder still on the stack and no payoff in hand. The BBB mana will likely go to waste if Ponder doesn't draw into something castable this turn. Dark Ritual is a powerful resource being spent speculatively before even seeing the Ponder draw. Even if they chain into Cabal Ritual, they'd have ~5 black mana with potentially nothing to spend it on.

Playing Windswept Heath instead of Karakas on turn 1 when they want to cast Aether Vial. With Karakas, they can tap for {W} and cast Aether Vial without spending any life or wasting a fetch land. With Windswept Heath, they either need to crack the fetch (losing 1 life and the future utility of the fetch) to get a Plains for Vial, or delay casting Vial.

The player should play Karakas from hand before passing. They have a land drop available (Karakas is in hand) and no land was played this turn. Missing a land drop is a clear mistake, especially when Karakas provides white mana and its legendary creature bounce ability could be relevant. Playing the land costs nothing and enables casting Swords to Plowshares or other spells next turn with two mana sources available.

Kimi25 Libby passed without activating Scalding Tarn. With Doomsday and Cabal Ritual in hand, they need to set up mana for a Doomsday turn. Cracking Scalding Tarn now to find an Island (Underground Sea or basic Swamp/Island) would give them access to more mana sources. With Underground Sea already on board and Scalding Tarn cracked for another land, they'd have 2 lands plus Cabal Ritual to potentially cast Doomsday next turn. The reasoning of 'waiting to see what the next draw reveals' doesn't make sense because this is already the main phase - they already drew for the turn. Cracking Tarn is free (costs 1 life) and thins the deck. There's no strategic reason to hold it - they can't cast anything this turn regardless, but getting the land onto the battlefield is pure upside for future turns. Additionally, with 5 cards in graveyard, cracking Tarn puts them at 6, getting closer to Threshold for Cabal Ritual.

Player could potentially cycle Edge of Autumn (sacrifice Scalding Tarn) to reach threshold (7 cards in graveyard), then tap Underground Sea for B, cast Cabal Ritual for BBBBB (threshold), and cast Doomsday for BBB with BB floating. This is a possible combo turn that was not explored. The opponent is developing with Stoneforge Mystic and waiting gives them more time to find disruption.

chosen_display: Stoneforge Mystic — {1}{W}, {T}: You may put an Equipment card from y... [Activate]
annotation_description: The player activated Stoneforge Mystic to put Pre-War Formalwear onto the battlefield before putting a charge counter on Aether Vial during upkeep. The Aether Vial trigger at the beginning of upkeep should be resolved first (putting it to 3 counters), which would allow vial-ing in Skyclave Apparition (3 mana value) at instant speed later. By using Stoneforge Mystic now (tapping Scrubland and Karakas for the {1}{W} cost), the player also loses access to Karakas's bounce ability for the turn. More importantly, the player should consider whether to let Aether Vial tick up first before committing to other actions during upkeep. However, the bigger issue is sequencing: activating Stoneforge during upkeep before the main phase is fine (it's instant speed), but the player should prioritize the Aether Vial upkeep trigger. The game engine likely handles the Vial trigger separately, so this may just be about using Stoneforge at the right time. Still, using Pre-War Formalwear now to reanimate Solitude (which has 3 or less mana value? No, Solitude is 5 MV) — actually Pre-War Formalwear returns a creature with MV 3 or less. The graveyard has Solitude (MV 5) and Windswept Heath (land). There's no valid creature with MV 3 or less in the graveyard to target with Pre-War Formalwear's ETB trigger, making the equipment somewhat wasted right now.

Failed to crack Scalding Tarn at the beginning of their own turn. With 5 cards in graveyard, cracking Tarn would put them at 6 (one away from Threshold for Cabal Ritual's bonus mode). More importantly, cracking Tarn into a second black source would enable the line: tap both lands for BB, cast Cabal Ritual (BBB), cast Doomsday. Even if Doomsday this turn isn't optimal without an immediate draw effect post-Doomsday, not cracking the fetch delays the combo and gives the opponent more time to develop with Stoneforge Mystic and Aether Vial.

Aether Vial currently has 2 charge counters (placed turn 1 and turn 2 upkeeps). The player has Skyclave Apparition in hand, which costs exactly {1}{W}{W} (mana value 3, not 2). However, there are no opponent creatures on the battlefield to target with Skyclave Apparition's ETB, so vialing it in now would be suboptimal anyway. The real issue is declining a free Aether Vial activation when it could put a creature into play. With 2 counters, there may not be a matching creature in hand (Skyclave is MV 3, Overlord is MV 5, Solitude is MV 5). Actually, checking the hand: Pre-War Formalwear (MV 3, not a creature), Swords to Plowshares (MV 1), Overlord of the Balemurk (MV 5), Skyclave Apparition (MV 3). None of these are MV 2 creatures, so declining the Vial activation is correct since there's nothing to put in. The decision to pass is reasonable.

Libby had 2 untapped Underground Seas (2 mana available) and could have cast Cabal Ritual ({1}{B}) to generate {B}{B}{B}, then cast Doomsday ({B}{B}{B}) this turn to set up a winning pile. Instead, Libby incorrectly believed only 1 mana was available and passed, giving the opponent another turn to develop with Stoneforge Mystic and Aether Vial.

Casting Cabal Ritual before Doomsday uses a valuable post-Doomsday resource for only 1 net extra black mana. Keeping Cabal Ritual in hand after Doomsday would give more flexibility to execute the 5-card pile, as it could generate mana on a future turn when threshold is more likely met.

Doomsday is on the stack resolving, which is one of the most dangerous combo spells in Legacy. The opponent is setting up a 5-card pile to win the game (typically with Thassa's Oracle or similar). Aether Vial has 2 charge counters (it's turn 4, and was played turn 1, so likely has ~3 counters, but even at 2 counters Skyclave Apparition costs 3). However, the critical missed opportunity is activating Aether Vial in response to Doomsday. If Vial has 3 counters, Skyclave Apparition could be put into play at instant speed — but there's nothing to exile with it yet since Doomsday is a sorcery on the stack. More importantly, the player should be considering whether any response is meaningful here. The real issue is that passing without any response to Doomsday — the premier combo spell — is questionable, but the available responses (Swords with no creature target, Vial with unclear counter count) may genuinely not help. However, if Aether Vial has enough counters, vialing in Skyclave Apparition in response could be relevant to have a body ready, and doing it at end of opponent's turn after Doomsday resolves would threaten to exile whatever combo piece they play. Not activating Vial here wastes the opportunity to deploy a threat while the opponent is tapped out.

During Doomsday pile construction, Lion's Eye Diamond was exiled instead of being included in the 5-card pile. LED is one of the most critical combo pieces for Doomsday piles, providing the mana needed to cast win conditions after drawing through the pile. Without LED, the pile likely cannot generate enough mana to execute a winning line, especially with only 2 tapped lands and a Lotus Petal for mana.

At the beginning of turn 4 upkeep, the player declined to act when they could have activated Aether Vial (currently at 2 counters from prior upkeeps, matching Stoneforge Mystic's MV) or activated Stoneforge Mystic to put Pre-War Formalwear onto the battlefield. The opponent is at 8 life after casting Doomsday (losing half their life), meaning they're on a tight Doomsday pile plan. Activating Stoneforge Mystic here to put Pre-War Formalwear into play (returning Solitude from graveyard) would create significant pressure and a removal effect, potentially disrupting whatever the opponent is trying to do with their Doomsday pile. Passing with no action wastes tempo in a critical window where the opponent is vulnerable at 8 life.

Cast Pre-War Formalwear for 3 mana with no valid creature target (MV 3 or less) in the graveyard - Solitude is MV 5 and Windswept Heath is a land. The ETB reanimation trigger is wasted. Against a post-Doomsday opponent at 8 life, maximizing pressure and holding interaction is critical. Additionally, even if they wanted the equipment, Stoneforge Mystic's activated ability could put it into play for only {1}{W} instead of hardcasting for {2}{W}.

After resolving Doomsday, the library is a precisely ordered 5-card pile. Casting Personal Tutor shuffles the library (cards 2-5 get randomized), destroying the carefully arranged Doomsday pile order. This likely ruins the entire combo line that Doomsday was setting up, wasting the 3 mana and half their life spent on Doomsday.

After resolving Doomsday, the library is a precisely ordered 5-card pile. Personal Tutor searches and SHUFFLES the library before putting the found card on top, which randomizes the remaining Doomsday pile cards and likely destroys the deterministic win sequence.

Opponent is at 6 life with no creatures to block. Attacking with only Stoneforge Mystic deals 1 damage instead of attacking with all creatures (Stoneforge Mystic 1/2, Phelia 2/2+, Skyclave Apparition 2/2) for at least 5 damage total, potentially lethal if Phelia has any +1/+1 counters or Pre-War Formalwear is equipped. Against a post-Doomsday opponent who is assembling a combo kill, failing to apply maximum pressure is game-losing.

annotation_description: Activated Aether Vial with no creature of the appropriate mana value in hand. The only creature in hand is Overlord of the Balemurk (MV 5), while Vial likely has 3 counters. The reasoning incorrectly states Skyclave Apparition is being put onto the battlefield, but it's already in play. This wastes the Vial tap for the turn.

Opponent is at 5 life. Timmy has Stoneforge Mystic (1/2), Skyclave Apparition (2/2), and Phelia, Exuberant Shepherd (2/2, likely with +1/+1 counters from flickering) on board with no opposing blockers. That's at minimum 5 power = exact lethal. Additionally, Overlord of the Balemurk costs {3}{B}{B} but Timmy only has one black source (Scrubland), making this cast appear impossible. Instead of going to combat for the kill, Timmy is trying to cast an expensive creature pre-combat.
